placeOrder runs persistence reads and writes: `this.customers.findById(customerId)`, `this.products.findBySku(item.sku)`, `this.products.updateStock(product.sku, product.stock)`, `this.orders.save(toOrderRecord(draft))`.
cancelOrder runs persistence I/O: `this.products.findBySku(line.sku)`, `this.products.updateStock(line.sku, record.stock + line.quantity)`, `this.orders.save(toOrderRecord(order))`.

parsedVerdict.reasoning: The rubric gives the business layer the domain kind. A domain file must not carry persistence or I/O responsibilities. The constructor-wiring exemption covers application files only, so it does not apply here. OrderService is a transaction script that runs persistence operations itself. Through gateway classes from src/persistence (infrastructure), it reads records (findById, findBySku) and writes them (save, updateStock). It also converts between domain objects and persistence records (toOrderRecord, toOrder, toProduct, toCustomer). Its constructor fields are typed directly as these concrete infrastructure gateways, not as ports declared in the domain. Import direction is out of scope. The finding is about what the file does: it orchestrates queries and writes, which is a persistence/I/O responsibility placed in a domain-kind file. The file has no HTTP or framework types and no decorators.

It also maps records (toOrderRecord/toOrder). Queries and writes belong to the infrastructure layer or to an application-layer orchestrator, not the domain.

The constructor fields `orders: OrderGateway`, `products: ProductGateway` and `customers: CustomerGateway` are typed as concrete persistence-layer (infrastructure) gateway types instead of ports declared in the domain. The domain class therefore depends on persistence clients.
